subtitle: Two wishes lead towards the same relic

body: Threads of Fate is Square's PlayStation action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 14 October 1999. Rue seeks an ancient relic to revive a dead friend, while the exiled princess Mint wants its power for a much less modest ambition. The player chooses one protagonist at the beginning, following a campaign shaped by that character's motives and abilities. Both journeys use the town of Carona and the surrounding areas, making the second viewpoint another way to understand familiar people and places. Their contrasting personalities give the adventure much of its humour and emotional range.

Combat takes place directly within three-dimensional environments, with exploration and small platforming challenges connecting the encounters. Rue and Mint bring different abilities to those spaces, changing how an obstacle or enemy can be handled. The hub town gives the player a place to return between newly opened areas, keeping the wider journey connected to a manageable group of locations. Playing the other campaign is therefore more than selecting a different face. The same setting becomes part of another character's problem, and abilities turn a remembered route into a different practical task.

Director and programmer Koji Sugimoto wanted a lighter tone after his work on Xenogears. The team also pursued a fully three-dimensional presentation without pre-rendered cinematic sequences, a demanding choice on PlayStation. Daisuke Watanabe wrote the script from Makoto Shimamoto's world design, with Junya Nakano composing the music. North America received the game in July 2000. Reviews generally welcomed its action and appearance, although sales disappointed. Its compact pair of adventures gives a clear form to the idea that the same wish-granting object can mean very different things to different people.
